HelpAge Ethiopia is a network member of HelpAge International, a global network of organizations working towards a fairer world for older people so they can live safe, healthy, and dignified lives. In addition to working with more than 170 network members in 91 countries, HelpAge International operates country program offices in 13 countries across Asia, Africa, the Middle East, and Eastern Europe. Over the years, the HelpAge International Ethiopia office has been engaging in various service provision activities including humanitarian and development assistance. HelpAge International has also played a key role in promoting the rights of older people and building the capacity of partners and stakeholders for sustainable change. These include setting up of advocacy framework and coordinating higher-level policy dialogues; strengthening the capacity of age- inclusive organizations and older people groups to own and demonstrate actions on and supporting consultative process between OPAs and CSO partners on a list of priority issues and agendas, facilitating them to take lead on the day-to-day implementation of project activities at local, district and regional levels. HelpAge International Ethiopia country program enjoys excellent rapport with the National and Local Government Authorities in Ethiopia including the Ministry of Health, Ministry of Women and Social Affairs, The Refugees and Returnees Service, Authority for Civil Society Organizations, and Regional Administration and Local Government structures. The country program also works with Government Institutions, Research/Academic Institutions, UN agencies, Network members, and Local partners based in Ethiopia. HelpAge International Ethiopia country program’s current focus areas are Income security, Healthy Ageing, and Inclusive Humanitarian Action. More specifically, our sectoral interventions address social protection, health and wellbeing, nutrition,voice/advocacy, livelihoods, protection, and inclusion in both humanitarian and development contexts. In line with its organizational commitment to the Charter for Change, a key element of the HelpAge International Global Strategy 2030, HelpAge International has been transitioning all country programs to be locally led and managed by national 2024/25. To this end, HelpAge International`s country office in Ethiopia has been undergoing a series of consultations for the past 3 years with stakeholders` including target beneficiaries to figure out the best option to embrace localization ambition.

Sida is Sweden's government agency for development cooperation. We strive to reduce poverty and oppression around the world. In cooperation with organisations, government agencies and the private sector we invest in sustainable development for all people.

TSDA was established in 2000 in Ethiopia to improve the lives of marginalised groups in the country, in particular vulnerable children, women, and older people living in poverty. TSDA designs and implements participatory projects that aim to prevent the spread of HIV/AIDS, and facilitate income generation and employment opportunities. TSDA has implemented various projects providing care and support for older people, community-based healthcare, education and learning, combating gender-based violence, and providing guidance to older people on how they can earn an income. It also provides food, shelter, and psychosocial and legal support, and is involved in fundraising, campaigning and advocacy. TSDA became a HelpAge global network member in 2018.

RLP is an outreach project for the School of Law, Makerere University, established in 1999 in response to research that indicated that refugees and asylum seekers do not fully enjoy their rights in Uganda. Its initial focus on the provision of Legal Aid and Psychosocial support to displaced people has since expanded and is now organised under five thematic programme areas;  Access to Justice  Conflict, Transitional Justice and Governance  Gender & Sexuality  Media for Social Change  Mental Health & Psychosocial Wellbeing Currently, RLP has ten (10) offices across the country with 167 employees with a gender disaggregation of 97Males and 70 Females from diverse backgrounds of professional disciplines, cultures and expertise, and with 32% of staff being refugees. RLP’s primary goal is to provide legal aid to refugees, asylum seekers, internally displaced persons and deportees. Over the years, RLP has grown into a ‘Leading Centre for Justice and Forced Migrants’, conducting cutting-edge research, evidence-based advocacy, and providing pro-bono legal aid services to forced migrants in various gazette refugee settlements refugee-hosting districts across Uganda. Vision RLP envisions a context where all people enjoy their human rights, irrespective of legal status. This vision is informed by relevant international laws and the Constitution of the Republic of Uganda. Mission RLP’s mission is to empower asylum seekers, refugees, deportees, IDPs and host communities to enjoy their human rights and lead dignified lives. Mandate RLP strikes to; 1. Promote the protection, well-being and dignity of displaced people and their hosts 2. Empower forced migrants, communities and all associated actors to challenge and combat injustices in policy, law and practice 3. Influence national and international debate on matters of forced migration, justice and peace 4. Be a resource for forced migrants and relevant actors. Core Values RLP’s core values are; i. Independence ii. Innovation iii. Non-discrimination iv. Respect v. Professionalism vi. Accountability vii. Rigour

Vision A future where Ethiopian women and girls fully exercise their rights, experience gender justice, and thrive in an equitable society. Mission To advance gender equality and build an equitable society for Ethiopian women and girls by delivering multi-dimensional programs in education, SRHR, skills development, community engagement, and advocacy, while leveraging strategic partnerships and innovative solutions in digitalization, science, and technology. EWDO Goal To contribute to an equitable, inclusive, and resilient society where women and girls, including vulnerable and older women, fully exercise their rights, live free from violence and discrimination, and actively participate in social and economic development with dignity and equal opportunity. EWDO Objectives 1. Digital Inclusion and Empowerment for Women and Girls: - EWDO works to close the digital gender gap by increasing women’s and girls’ access to technology, digital skills, and online opportunities. The pillar also promotes online safety and addresses technology-facilitated violence; ensuring digital spaces support education, livelihoods, and empowerment. 2. Specialized GBV Prevention, Response, and Access to Justice: To prevent and respond to gender-based violence (GBV) and harmful practices by strengthening survivor-centered services, protection systems, access to justice, and community awareness. 3. Access to Comprehensive Sexual and Reproductive Health and Rights (SRHR): To improve equitable access to comprehensive sexual and reproductive health and rights (SRHR) information and services, particularly for marginalized and underserved women and girls. 4. Socio-Economic Empowerment and Leadership: EWDO strengthens women’s economic independence through skills development, entrepreneurship, and digital inclusion including elder people, marginalized and underserved groups. The pillar also promotes women’s leadership across sectors, enabling them to influence economic and social decision-making. 5. Peace, Governance, and Humanitarian Action: EWDO supports active participation of women and vulnerable groups in peace building, governance, and humanitarian response. The organization advocates for gender-responsive systems and uses innovative and digital approaches to ensure women’s voices and needs are central in crisis and recovery efforts. 6. Organizational Excellence and Sustainable Impact: To strengthen institutional capacity, partnerships, innovation, and evidence-based programming to ensure sustainable impact and organizational excellence.
